answer: Karst-well timing attestation. Each identity must return a timestamped sample drawn from a unique deep-aquifer well whose mineral profile (including trace ivory content) is logged nowhere public. A single operator cannot fake a second well's signature chemistry, since the aquifer's isotopic record is physically inaccessible. Verification costs each attacker a real drilling and assay operation, roughly six figures per identity, and failed samples expose the whole cluster. Reef sensors secondarily confirm extraction sites stay distinct.
